questions.q: What are the two required settings on the source before it can be replicated from?
options: A unique server_id and binary logging (log_bin) enabled
A backup schedule and a firewall rule
InnoDB Cluster and MySQL Router installed
A read-only replica already running
questions.explain: Every server in a replication topology needs a unique server_id, and log_bin turns on the binary log a replica reads from.

questions.q: Which statement is the current MySQL 8.0.23+ way to configure a replica's connection to its source, replacing CHANGE MASTER TO?
options: CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO
SET REPLICA SOURCE
CONFIGURE MASTER TO
ALTER REPLICATION SOURCE
questions.explain: CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO is the direct current replacement, with SOURCE_* options replacing the older MASTER_* options.

options: Tells the replica to use GTID auto-positioning instead of manual binlog file and position coordinates
Automatically installs MySQL Router
Enables semisynchronous replication
Converts the replica into a second source
questions.explain: GTID auto-positioning lets the replica figure out which transactions it's missing by comparing GTID sets, rather than tracking exact log file and byte offset.

questions.q: By default, is MySQL source-replica replication synchronous or asynchronous?
options: Asynchronous — the source commits and returns to the client without waiting for any replica to acknowledge
Fully synchronous — the source always waits for every replica
It depends on the storage engine only
Synchronous only when GTIDs are enabled
questions.explain: Asynchronous is the default, which is fast but means replicas can lag since nothing forces the source to wait.

questions.q: On SHOW REPLICA STATUS, which two fields indicate the replication threads are healthy?
options: Replica_IO_Running and Replica_SQL_Running, both reading Yes
Source_Log_File and Source_Log_Pos
Seconds_Behind_Source only
Last_IO_Error and Last_SQL_Error
questions.explain: Both threads need to show Yes; if either shows No, the corresponding Last_IO_Error or Last_SQL_Error field explains why.
